usage: This is the standard, everyday way to say you are busy in Moroccan Darija. It is used in both formal and casual contexts. The adjective must agree with the speaker's gender, so a female speaker will use the feminine form.

variants.label: female speaker
variants.note: Used when the person speaking is a woman.

variants.label: group
variants.note: Used when speaking on behalf of a group.

variants.label: idiomatic alternative
variants.note: A very common phrase literally meaning 'I have what is to be done'.

examples.arabic: مَا نْقْدَرْش نْخْرَج لْيُوم، أَنَا مَشْغُول.
examples.transliteration: ma nqdersh nkherj lyoum, ana mshghoul.
examples.english: I can't go out today, I'm busy.

examples.arabic: عَيَّط لِيَّا مَنْ بَعْد، أَنَا مَشْغُول دَابَا.
examples.transliteration: 3eyyet liya men be3d, ana mshghoul daba.
examples.english: Call me later, I'm busy right now.

examples.arabic: سْمَح لِيَّا، أَنَا مَشْغُول مْعَا لْخَدْمَة.
examples.transliteration: sme7 liya, ana mshghoul m3a lkhedma.
